subject: Post-call: Montec evaluation — equivalence thresholds, prompt bundle & pilot plan
messages:
From: Caroline Mercer <caroline@montec.ai>

Cc: procurement@montec.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up / next steps from today

Thanks for the walkthrough today, Mina — good call. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- We liked the latency/cost tradeoffs you showed for batched workloads; the team is concerned about occasional hallucination spikes on multi-step SOP generation.
- Security: our procurement team will send a standard questionnaire (SOC2 items + data retention).
- Pilot ask: we want a short, instrumented pilot to compare your open-model candidates vs our internal baseline (we'll call it "Montec v1" internally).

Can you send a recommended evaluation plan (metrics, prompt sets, acceptance thresholds) and an example prompt bundle we can sanity-check? Also, rough SOW/credits estimate so procurement can budget.

Best,
Caroline Mercer
Head of Integrations, Montec AI
caroline@montec.ai

Montec AI | https://montec.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Mercer <caroline@montec.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up / next steps from today

Caroline — great meeting, thanks. Attaching a concise pilot proposal and the initial prompt bundle for Montec to review. High-level summary below:

1) Recommended model slate to trial (open candidates):
   - Mistral-Instruct-22B (fp16) — strong instruction-following; lower cost for short responses
   - Llama-3-70B (8k window, quantized 4-bit) — better multi-step coherence for long SOP generation
   - OpenChain-EncDec-Chat (experimental) — try if you need structured outputs / tables

2) Proprietary baseline: Montec v1 — we propose you run a short set of prompts against this baseline; our acceptance check will compare quality and hallucination rate against it.

3) Acceptance / equivalence thresholds (proposal):
   - Primary: Task-specific accuracy / pass rate >= 0.95 of Montec v1 on canonical prompt set
   - Hallucination: factual hallucination rate <= Montec v1 + 2 percentage points on the corpus of 200 verification queries
   - Fluency & instruction following: human-rated quality (1–5) mean >= 4.0 AND delta <= 0.2 vs Montec v1
   - Latency: p95 token latency <= 1.25x Montec v1 for synchronous calls (configurable for batching)

4) Benchmarks & artifacts provided: prompt bundle (attached), evaluation matrix (attached), Drive folder with token-level latency/cost examples: https://drive.google.com/montec/eval-benchmarks

5) Pilot scope & timeline (suggested):
   - 2-week instrumented trial, 1 model per week (week 1: Mistral-Instruct, week 2: Llama-3-70B)
   - Daily sampling of outputs, weekly human-review on 50 sampled prompts
   - Automated checks for hallucination and factual consistency with your verification set

6) Commercial / SOW: draft SOW attached (credits for trial + optional extended support). Rishi, can you propose a credit + SOW outline? Evelyn, happy to have you own the success/readouts during the trial.

Next actions:
- Caroline: confirm pilot length and whether Montec will provide the Montec v1 sandbox endpoints + verification set (200 items).
- Procurement: please review attached SOW draft.

We can also run a short pre-trial smoke test (24–48h) if you want to sanity-check keys and routing.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0134

Attachments: montec_trial_prompt_bundle_v1.json (prompt set, eval labels), evaluation_matrix_v2.xlsx (metric definitions + scoring rules), redwood_trial_sow_draft.pdf
From: Caroline Mercer <caroline@montec.ai>

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications:

- We can provide Montec v1 sandbox and the verification set by EOD Thursday.
- Pilot length: OK to start with the 2-week pilot. We'll ask procurement to sign the SOW (attached) and will push for a single PO to cover the trial credits.
- Hallucination check: can you share the automated script you use to compute the 'factual hallucination rate' so our data team can replicate?

Procurement note: I attached our standard questionnaire (SOC2 + retention). If you could confirm roughly which items require a longer lead time (e.g., encryption key rotation docs), that would help.

Can we kick off with a smoke test on Friday to validate keys and routing?

Cheers,
Caroline
